subject: ferrets
one_liner: On-demand transit for domesticated ferrets, dispatched through the wall cavities, floor voids, and appliance gaps of participating residences.
brand_voice_notes: Straight-faced infrastructure company. Slink talks about a pet moving through a wall the way a transit authority talks about a corridor: surveyed, priced, scheduled, and audited. The joke is never acknowledged. Copy is clipped and procedural, borrowing the register of a mechanical drawing set and a fare schedule. Every absurdity is stated as a resolved operational fact, and the only warmth in the writing is misplaced pride in the routing. Numbers are specific and slightly too precise. Nothing is ever apologized for, least of all the insulation.

hero.h1: Your ferret already knows a shorter way
hero.sub: Slink is on-demand transit for domesticated ferrets, dispatched through the wall cavities, floor voids, and appliance gaps of participating residences. Median pickup, 40 seconds. Median arrival, unresolved.

features.title: Cavity-aware routing
features.blurb: We surveyed 11,400 homes and logged every void a ferret can physically enter. Slink picks the shortest one. Whether your ferret should be inside a load-bearing wall is a question the router does not ask.

features.title: Dook verification
features.blurb: Drivers authenticate by vocalization. We sample the dook at pickup and match it against a voiceprint index of 2.1 million clips. Impersonation is down 12 percent. Dooking is up 400 percent.

features.title: Dynamic vent pricing
features.blurb: Demand behind the dryer peaks between 18:00 and 20:00, and Slink prices it honestly. Riders who wait for the cycle to finish save 60 percent and arrive warm.

pricing_tiers.name: Baseboard
pricing_tiers.tagline: Shared cavity. You may be matched with up to four other ferrets and one draft nobody has accounted for.

pricing_tiers.name: Ductwork Priority
pricing_tiers.tagline: Conditioned air, direct routing, slightly warm on arrival.

pricing_tiers.name: Load-Bearing
pricing_tiers.tagline: Structural access. Requires written landlord consent, which we collect and do not read.

demo_screen_concept: A live dispatch console for one residence, drawn as a whiteprint cutaway: a CSS/SVG section through a two-storey house with the cavity network overlaid as clickable route segments (baseboard runs, stud bays, the dryer vent, the under-sink shortcut), each labelled with a clearance in millimetres. Left rail holds the matched driver card with a dook-signature waveform, star rating, and vehicle line reading 'Sable jill, 41 cm, no collar'. Right rail holds a fare breakdown that recomputes on every reroute (base, cavity surcharge, insulation, dook verification levy) and an ETA that only ever increases. Route-preference toggles (avoid insulation, avoid the cat, allow structural, permit chimney) flip segments in and out of service and force a live reroute. A surge chip pulses on the dryer vent. Below, a scrolling trip log of completed slinks with outcomes like 'ARRIVED, WRONG FLOOR' and 'RIDER ASLEEP IN TRANSIT'.

design_direction.style: Diazo whiteprint drawing set, ozalid daylight mode. The page is staged as the issued drawing package of a heavily funded transportation company that has decided the domestic wall cavity is an unbuilt transit corridor and files your ferret under conveyance. A warm ozalid paper ground (#E8E4D8) runs the whole page with no gradients, no glow, no glass, no blur, and no shadows of any kind: every division is a 1px prussian hairline or a hard hatch fill, corners are 2px, and structure comes entirely from ruled plates and the grid of a drawing sheet. The organizing move is the sheet: each section is a titled plate with a corner title block (DWG NO. / REV / SCALE / SHEET) and a wide-tracked mono caption, so the reader is scrolling a drawing set rather than a website. The core motif is the section cut: a 45-degree hairline hatch built in repeating-linear-gradient, used wherever the page shows a wall in cutaway, and reused as the fill behind plate headers, the active pricing tier, and the hero slab, so the whole site looks cut open. The second motif is the dimension line: a prussian rule terminated by arrow ticks with a numeral floating in a break at its centre, used as the section divider, the list bullet, the fare unit, the ETA readout, and the clearance label on every cavity, so every quantity on the page is presented as a measurement taken off a drawing. One prussian blue (#1B3B6F) carries the wordmark, all linework, every primary CTA, and one word per headline, always as a solid flood with paper knocked out of it. One rationed survey orange (#C8471F) is quarantined strictly to live dispatch telemetry (surge chips, the travelling route dot, active-trip states, the ETA when it increases, unresolved arrivals) and appears nowhere else, so the only warm colour on the sheet is always something dispatch is worried about. Chivo sets the wordmark and headlines in sturdy municipal grotesque with infrastructure-company-that-raised-a-C confidence, tracking tightened to -0.02em at display sizes; Atkinson Hyperlegible carries plain, faintly permit-application body copy. Every figure that pretends to be dispatch telemetry (clearances in millimetres, fares, ETAs, cavity IDs, dook match scores, tier prices) is set in Azeret Mono with tabular figures inside hairline-ruled paper wells, so it reads like the schedule of quantities, not marketing. Motion is drafting-restrained: dimension lines draw out from their centre once on scroll, hatch fills shift 4px on hover with the hairline darkening, the route dot travels its cavity path on a 6s loop, CTAs depress 1px on press, plates fade up 6px with a 40ms stagger, all gated behind prefers-reduced-motion. No dark mode, no glass, no blur panels, no clay shadow pairs, no bento lattice, no aurora washes, no offset sticker shadows, no catalog stitching, no didone engraving, no split-flap numerals, no racing-form condensed type, no mirrored type, no storefront capsules, no engraved seals, no emoji. Reads like a company that files your home under 'right of way' and considers the stud bay an underused asset.

design_direction.archetype: Consumer on-demand transport product page issued as a mechanical drawing set: hero plate with a monumental grotesque claim beside a CSS-built wall-cutaway section showing a live route, a dispatch telemetry strip in dimension lines, three feature plates with title blocks, testimonial plates with ID-photo headshots and driver numbers, a three-tier fare schedule with the middle tier hatched as issued-for-construction, closing CTA band, handoff to the dispatch console demo.
design_direction.motion_vocab: Dimension lines draw out from their centre on scroll; hatch fills shift 4px on hover with the hairline darkening to prussian; the survey-orange route dot travels its cavity path on a 6s loop; CTAs depress 1px on press; plates fade up 6px with a 40ms stagger; every animation gated behind prefers-reduced-motion.
design_direction.hero_composition_notes: Two-column plate on ozalid paper. Left: a wide-tracked mono sheet caption (SHEET A-01 / CAVITY NETWORK, TYP.), the monumental Chivo headline with one word flooded prussian, permit-register subcopy, the primary CTA beside a mono clearance readout, and a dimension line hemming the block. Right: a CSS-built cutaway section through a wall, drywall faces drawn as hairlines, the stud bay hatched at 45 degrees, a survey-orange dot travelling the cavity on a 6s loop with a clearance dimension called out beside it. A title block sits at the plate's bottom-right corner. Collapses to a single column under 900px with the cutaway sitting below the headline.
